newsitem.title: INDIA: India Century Tex falls 7.3 pct.
newsitem.headline: India Century Tex falls 7.3 pct.

text.p: Shares of Century Textiles and Industries Ltd dropped 7.3 percent on Friday, taking the fall to 21.5 percent since Monday, after the firm said its profits plunged 99 percent, brokers said.
The share was down 148.25 rupees, or 7.29 percent, at 1,885 on the Bombay Stock Exchange. On Monday, it had closed at 2,401.
The diversified firm said on Tuesday its net profits tumbled to 26.7 million rupees in the year ended March 31, 1997, from 1.9 billion a year ago.

A 218.6 percent jump in interest and finance costs to 1.63 billion rupees from 510.7 million in 1995/96, sluggish cement and paper markets, weak dry bulk freight rates in shipping and acute electricity shortages hit operations, the firm said.

The flagship firm of B.K. Birla group had raised $100 million through a global depositary receipt (GDR) issue in 1994. In 1996/97 it had put off a $125 million GDR issue due to poor market conditions.
Despite the fall in profits the company's directors said on Tuesday they had recommended a bonus equity issue in the proportion of one share for every share held.
